definitions.explanation: controlling one's emotions, desires, or impulses through willpower

examples.japanese: {怒|いか}りを{感|かん}じたが、なんとか{自制|じせい}した。
examples.english: I felt anger but managed to restrain myself.

examples.japanese: ダイエット{中|ちゅう}は{自制心|じせいしん}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
{彼|かれ}は{常|つね}に{自制|じせい}の{効|き}いた{態度|たいど}を{崩|くず}さない。
examples.english: He always maintains a composed, self-controlled attitude.

notes:
{自制|じせい} means controlling oneself, particularly one's emotions, desires, or impulses.

KANJI BREAKDOWN:
- {自|じ} (self)
- {制|せい} (control, regulate)

USAGE:
- {自制|じせい}する (to exercise self-control - suru verb)
- {自制心|じせいしん} (self-control, willpower - noun)
- {自制|じせい}を{失|うしな}う (to lose self-control)
- {自制|じせい}が{効|き}く (to have self-control working)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {自制|じせい}を{保|たも}つ (to maintain self-control)
- {自制|じせい}を{促|うなが}す (to urge self-restraint)
- {自制|じせい}の{効|き}いた (self-controlled, composed)

NUANCE:
- More internal/psychological than {抑制|よくせい} (restraint)
- Implies conscious effort and willpower
- Can refer to controlling emotions, appetite, spending, etc.

RELATED TERMS:
- {抑制|よくせい} (restraint, suppression)
- {忍耐|にんたい} (patience, endurance)
- {節制|せっせい} (moderation, temperance)
- {我慢|がまん} (patience, self-control)
